Four always-running sequencing tests were added; they use a recording post seam, so none of them can move the real cursor.

cursorObservationCorrection.finding: Root reviewer finding: the probe mapped its cursor read-back with 'switch CGEvent(source: nil)?.location { case .some(origin): ... }', a pattern the reviewer judged unsafe because it may be read as binding a new identifier rather than comparing with the captured origin, which would report every non-nil read-back as matchesOrigin.
cursorObservationCorrection.change: The mapping was extracted into the pure helper manualProbeCursorObservation(readBack:origin:), which compares with explicit ==, and the probe now calls it. One always-running test, cursorObservationComparesTheReadBackWithTheOrigin, covers the equal, different and nil read-backs. The real probe was not run.

cursorSafety.claim: No automated test posted a CGEvent, so no automated test could move the real cursor.
cursorSafety.how: Every test that reaches the post step substitutes MacMouseMoveInjectionEnvironment.postEvent with a recording closure. The two tests that touch production defaults cannot reach posting: productionDefaultResolvesNoPlatformPositionSoNothingIsEverPosted stops at the permission check or at the unresolved resolver, and liveEnvironmentCreatesAMouseMovedEventAtTheRequestedPositionAndPostsNothing invokes only the live creation closure, which the SDK documents as allocation. The probe that can post is skipped unless MACKVM_M1_036_MANUAL_PROBE is set.
